lede: The biggest thing on the civic calendar this week is the San Miguel County BOCC's triple-header of public hearings on August 5 — three Land Use Code amendments up for formal action, including changes to 'Qualified Owner' definitions and a wildfire-areas update, all open for public comment. The Open Space Commission kicks things off Monday with a real decision on the Valley Floor River Trail alignment. The Housing Authority Subcommittee weighs in on whether a deed-restricted owner can replace a roof that blows past her improvement cap, and Mountain Village's Design Review Board takes up three multifamily projects Thursday.

notable.stake: Commissioners pick one of three River Trail alignments near Valley Floor wetlands.
Vote on whether deed-restricted owner can exceed improvement cap for a new roof.
Three public hearings on Land Use Code changes, including wildfire rules and owner definitions.
Definition changes to Ouray County Land Use Code could quietly shift what gets permitted.
Three multifamily projects, including a conditional-use permit, go before Mountain Village DRB.
